/.title: Annoying Goods — Writing Studio and AI Tools
/.description: Annoying Goods is a spider-themed studio building AGIT, AGrrr!, AGnosis and AGDevelop: honest tools for writers and researchers who keep notes in the dark.

/about/.description: About the Annoying Goods studio: a small team building honest writing and research tools, the mission behind the products, and how the studio thinks about work.

/about/philosophy/.description: The Annoying Goods philosophy: build fewer things, keep them honest, let the craft show, and never pretend a tool is smarter than the person holding it.

/about/principles/.description: The working principles behind every Annoying Goods product, written as a numbered list you can argue with: privacy first, no dark patterns, real documentation.

/about/what-and-why/.description: What Annoying Goods builds and why: writing and research software for people who would rather own a quiet tool than rent a loud one. Here is the reasoning.

/products/.description: Every Annoying Goods product in one place: AGIT, AGrrr!, AGnosis, AGDevelop, yAGna, AGony and AG-web, plus the playground. One line per product with a link.

/products/agit/.description: AGIT is a free local-first writing app: chat, editor, outline and boards for fiction, non-fiction, research and role-play, with AI that never owns your words.

/products/agit/features/.description: Every AGIT feature on one page: fiction, non-fiction, research, role-play and external tools, each with a plain summary and a link to the full explanation.

/products/agit/features/fiction/.description: AGIT for fiction: draft long work in the editor, keep characters and chapters in the outline, and switch to a scene board when the story misbehaves. See it.

/products/agit/features/non-fiction/.description: AGIT for non-fiction: turn rough research into structured notes, draft essays and reports, and keep every source attached to the claim it supports. See it.

/products/agit/features/research/.description: AGIT for research: import, index, compute and chart, connect external tools, and automate the boring parts. It explains the four workflows and where they lead.
/products/agit/features/research/.title: AGIT Research — Annoying Goods

/products/agit/features/research/import-.description: How AGIT imports and indexes: bring in documents, notes and links, let the local index map your sources, then move from raw material to structured notes.

/products/agit/features/research/compute.description: Compute and chart in AGIT: paste text and get word counts, sentence lengths and top terms with a live chart. The demo runs in your browser and uploads nothing.

/products/agit/features/research/mcp-and.description: Connect AGIT to external tools through the Model Context Protocol, so research helpers can read and write where you already work. The contract and the limits.

/products/agit/features/research/automat.description: Automation recipes for AGIT research: named examples with clear inputs and outputs, so you can see what a repeatable pipeline looks like before you build one.

/products/agit/features/role-play/.description: Role-play in AGIT: two ways to use it, one for writing and one for fun. This index explains what each variant is for and points to the page that goes deeper.

/products/agit/features/role-play/rolepl.description: Role-play for writing in AGIT: rehearse a difficult scene, argue a position, or hear a character's voice before you commit it to the page. With a scene outline.
Role-play for fun in AGIT: a separate, casual set of uses with nothing to do with the writing workflow, kept apart so serious work and idle play never blur.

/products/agit/features/external-tools/.description: External tools with AGIT: how the writing and research workspace talks to the rest of your machine, what data crosses the boundary, and how to stay in control.

/products/agit/comparison/.description: Compare AGIT editions and plans against each other, feature by feature, with no competitor names and no invented claims. A plain table of what ships in each.

/products/agit/download/.description: Download AGIT: version numbers, supported platforms, file sizes and checksum placeholders for each build, with the licence and system requirements listed first.

/products/agit/privacy/.description: The AGIT privacy policy: the English and Polish versions of the product privacy text, and a plain note on which version prevails if the two ever disagree.
/products/agit/privacy/.title: AGIT Privacy Policy — Annoying Goods

/products/agit/privacy/en/.description: The English AGIT privacy policy: exactly what the writing tool stores, where it stores it, whether anything leaves your machine, and the rights you keep.

/products/agit/privacy/pl/.description: Polska wersja polityki prywatności AGIT: co narzędzie zapisuje, gdzie to przechowuje, czy cokolwiek opuszcza Twój komputer oraz jakie prawa zachowujesz.

/products/agrrr/.description: AGrrr! is the Annoying Goods page-builder with teeth: throw raw drafts at a live canvas, get real HTML and CSS back, and keep every growl on your own machine.

/products/agnosis/.description: One hotkey and every open browser minimizes behind a fullscreen ASCII duck parade: AGnosis, the joke that ships. No accounts, no cloud, nothing ever closed.

/products/agdevelop/.description: AGDevelop is an Annoying Goods product in development: a short, honest description of what it is meant to do, and a link to the request form if you want a say.

/labs/.description: The Annoying Goods labs: how an idea travels from rough prototype to alpha, to a working pipeline, or to the failed shelf. The index explains every stage.

/labs/prototypes/.description: Prototypes in the Annoying Goods labs: rough, disposable experiments built to answer one question at a time. What each prototype was testing, and why it failed.

/labs/alpha/.description: Alpha builds in the Annoying Goods labs: usable but unstable, with features that may change or disappear without warning. Try them and tell us what broke.

/labs/failed/.description: The failed shelf in the Annoying Goods labs: archived experiments with a one-line post-mortem for each, kept so the studio remembers what did not work.

/labs/workflow/.description: How an idea moves through the Annoying Goods labs, from the first throwaway prototype to alpha, then to a repeatable workflow or the failed shelf. The pipeline.

/blog/.description: The Annoying Goods blog: dev updates, release notes, technical dives and design decisions from a small studio building writing and research tools in the open.

/blog/dev-updates/.description: Dev updates from the Annoying Goods studio: what moved this week, what broke, what is still a mess and what happens next. Short notes, written as we go.

/blog/release-notes/.description: Release notes for Annoying Goods products: every shipped version with its number, what changed, what got fixed and what broke. Plain changelog, newest first.

/blog/technical-dives/.description: Technical dives from the Annoying Goods studio: long reads on indexing, statistics, the WebAssembly chart engine and the small decisions behind a fast site.

/blog/design-decisions/.description: Design decisions from the Annoying Goods studio: why the site is static, why a theme pill replaced the old toggle, and why the chart demo runs locally.

/blog/other/.description: Other writing from the Annoying Goods studio: the posts that do not fit dev updates, release notes, technical dives or design decisions. Notes and bug stories.

/words/.description: Words from Annoying Goods: short stories, AI stories and research notes published by the studio, each with a standfirst, an author note and a preview.

/words/short-stories/.description: Short stories from Annoying Goods: original fiction with a standfirst, a preview of the opening words and an author note. Read the start of each story.

/words/ai-stories/.description: AI stories from Annoying Goods: fiction written with machines in the loop, published with a plain note on how each piece was made and what the author kept.

/words/research/.description: Research notes from Annoying Goods: sourced writing on the tools, models and workflows the studio studies, with the method stated up front and sources listed.
/words/research/.title: Research Notes — Annoying Goods

/support/.description: Support for Annoying Goods: answers to common questions, the public source, the privacy policy and the terms of use. Every page is written to be read once.

/support/faq/.description: Frequently asked questions about Annoying Goods and its products: what AGIT does, what the cookie banner stores, how the chart demo handles your text,

/support/github/.description: Where the Annoying Goods source lives and how it is laid out: the static site, the stylesheets, the TypeScript modules, the build tools and the WASM crate.

/support/privacy-policy/.description: The Annoying Goods privacy policy in plain language: what is collected, what stays on your device, how a form submission is handled, how to delete your data.
/support/privacy-policy/.title: Privacy Policy — Annoying Goods

/support/terms-of-use/.description: The terms of use for the Annoying Goods website: the rules for using the site, the forms and the demo, the responsibilities you take on, and what we promise.

/contact/.description: Contact the Annoying Goods studio: two routes, one to report bugs and one to request features. Pick one and write clearly, and it reaches our mailbox.

/contact/report-bug/.description: Report a bug to Annoying Goods: give the product, a short summary, the steps to reproduce it, what you expected and what happened. Precise reports get fixed.

/contact/request-feature/.description: Request a feature for an Annoying Goods product: name the product area, give the idea a title, describe it plainly with the use case. One idea per message.

/products/yagna/.title: yAGna — Annoying Goods
/products/yagna/.description: yAGna is a local-first GitHub stars library written in Rust: every starred repo offline with READMEs, licenses, tags, a health index, search and digests.

/products/agony/.title: AGony — Annoying Goods
/products/agony/.description: AGony is a desktop environment that lives in a terminal: windows, a taskbar, a start menu and a command bar that suggests everything, built in Rust on rmux.

/products/ag-web/.title: AG-web — Annoying Goods
/products/ag-web/.description: AG-web is the studio site itself: dependency-free HTML and CSS with TypeScript and Rust where needed, assembled by its own build and served from IONOS.

/playground/.title: Playground — Annoying Goods
/playground/.description: The Annoying Goods playground: four slots for small games and tiny WebAssembly experiments, each on its own page with a stripped-down, static layout of its own.

/playground/one/.title: drAGhts — Annoying Goods
/playground/one/.description: drAGhts is chaotic checkers with eight house rules: play hot-seat with a friend or face the computer, online in the playground or from an offline archive.

/playground/two/.title: Playground Slot Two — Annoying Goods
/playground/two/.description: Playground slot two is reserved for the second small game or tiny WebAssembly experiment. The black stage box is in place and waiting for its first build.

/playground/nAG/.title: nAG — Annoying Goods
/playground/nAG/.description: nAG is a reverse-order memory game: scout the shuffled board, then replay the whole order in one perfect run. Play it online or download it to play offline.

/products/nAG/.title: nAG, the memory game that nags you — Annoying Goods
/products/nAG/.description: Get nAG, the reverse-order memory game: scout the board, then replay the whole order in one perfect run. A small archive that plays offline in any browser.

/products/nAG/download/.title: Download nAG — Annoying Goods
/products/nAG/download/.description: Download nAG, the reverse-order memory game. One small archive with the whole game in it: unzip it, open index.html and play the game offline in any browser.

/products/agony/features/.title: AGony Features — Annoying Goods
/products/agony/features/.description: Every AGony feature on its own page: the command bar, the window manager, the start menu with its app directory, the file panel, and the settings and themes.

/products/agony/features/command-bar/.title: AGony Command Bar — Annoying Goods
/products/agony/features/command-bar/.description: Press Ctrl-K and the AGony command bar suggests app names, your run history, file paths and completions for a thousand commands. Nothing runs on its own.

/products/agony/features/windows/.title: AGony Windows — Annoying Goods
/products/agony/features/windows/.description: AGony gives the terminal real windows: drag them, resize them, minimize to the taskbar, and the shells keep running when the desktop closes. A real capture.

/products/agony/features/start-menu/.title: AGony Start Menu — Annoying Goods
/products/agony/features/start-menu/.description: The AGony start menu has four roots (search, file manager, programs, settings) and its directory installs curated terminal apps via winget, scoop or cargo.

/products/agony/features/file-panel/.title: AGony File Panel — Annoying Goods
/products/agony/features/file-panel/.description: The AGony file panel is a gitignore-aware tree beside your shells. Grab a file, drop it into the command bar, and pick name, absolute or relative path there.

/products/agony/features/settings/.title: AGony Settings and Themes — Annoying Goods
/products/agony/features/settings/.description: AGony has three themes with per-role recoloring that refuses low-contrast picks, live preview until Apply, key rebinding with collision checks, plus ASCII mode.

/products/agony/download/.title: AGony Download — Annoying Goods
/products/agony/download/.description: Download AGony 0.9.0: the Windows archive with size and SHA-256 checksum, the two free prerequisites (the rmux engine and carapace), and honest platform notes.

/products/agony/license/.title: AGony License — Annoying Goods
/products/agony/license/.description: AGony is Apache-2.0: use it, study it, change it and ship it, commercially or not, as long as the license and notices travel along. Dependencies credited here.

/products/agony/comparison/.title: AGony Comparison — Annoying Goods
/products/agony/comparison/.description: AGony against tmux, Zellij and Windows Terminal in one honest table, feature by feature, with the rows included where those established tools still beat it.

/products/drAGhts/.description: Get drAGhts, chaotic checkers with eight toggleable house rules: play a friend hot-seat or face the computer, in the browser or from a small offline archive.

/products/drAGhts/download/.title: Download drAGhts — Annoying Goods
